text.p: Gold prices slid to 18-month lows overnight amid overwhelmingly bearish market sentiment, and analysts said it still had room to fall further.
Prices for industrial metals also took another dive as consumers backed off and waited for lower values.
On the LME prices for aluminium fell to 2-1/4 year lows, lead slumped to a fresh seven-month nadir, tin was its weakest for sixteen months and nickel fell to a two-month low.
The flagship copper contract extended recent sharp losses to around US$100 from late last week to $1,890 and only zinc showed a semblance of stability.
In Chicago, improved weather for seeding the U.S. winter wheat crop and another sharp drop in soybeans drove CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
The CRB index closed 1.43 points lower at 244.20.

New York precious metals futures ended slightly higher Tuesday, helped by some fund shortcovering, but the downtrend of the past month remains intact, traders said. "Sentiment is still bearish," Credit Suisse New York-based vice president Ian MacDonald said. "The IMF postponed a decision on gold sales this week, but there is a feeling central bank activity remains a cloud over the market, while physical demand from industry is not picking up in line with usual seasonal patterns and U.S. dollar strength is not helping either," he said. COMEX December gold ended up 50 cents at $381.00 an ounce, after trading in a $379.00-381.50 range. In New York bullion trade, spot gold ended quoted around $378.60 an ounce, compared with the London afternoon fix at $378.65, and up from the morning fix at $377.05, the lowest since March 6, 1995.

Copper prices fell sharply on the London Metal Exchange after a hefty drop in stocks failed to underpin the market. Other base metals fell in copper's wake, dragged down by speculative selling and bearish sentiment as well as a lack of consumer buying interest. Three month copper futures finished the afternoon kerb at $1,890 a tonne, down $38 from Monday's close and at the low of the day. The market peaked at $1990 late last week. The bearish mood in copper soon spread to other markets, where funds and speculators liquidated long positions and adopted fresh short ones, traders said. Consumers were sidelined in the expectation of more losses. Aluminium eased $10 to $1,367.50 having posted a fresh 2-1/4 year low of $1,357 earlier in the day. Lead sunk to a seven-month low but ended higher at $757. Nickel slumped to a two-month low of $7,000 and ended close to the nadir at $7,005, down $95.

Improved weather for seeding the U.S. winter wheat crop and another sharp drop in soybeans drove CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said. "It was more fund liquidation," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "Funds usually liquidate for two or three days in a row so we'll see what tomorrow brings." Weather forecasts for the U.S. Midwest indicated conditions more conducive for seeding the 1997 U.S. winter wheat crop. Wheat closed one to 3-3/4 cents per bushel lower, with December down 2-1/4 at $4.33-3/4. March was 3-3/4 lower at $4.18-3/4.

NYMEX crude ended lower Tuesday on talk of new supply as Iraq expressed hope its oil-for-food deal may be implemented soon and oil sales from the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve were approved by the U.S. Senate. November crude oil settled off 24 cents at $24.14 a barrel after falling as low as $23.83.

CSCE world sugar futures settled weaker and at the day's lows as speculators continued to pressure the market, floor sources said. March closed 0.11 weaker at 10.78, having ranged from 10.93 to 10.76. Back months finished 0.09 to 0.06 lower.
